headline: Two Plays, Two Losses, One Perfectly Round Twenty Dollar Hole
paragraphs: Four games hit the grader this week. The model looked at two of them, shrugged, and bet the other two for ten dollars each. Both lost. That is a 0-2 week, 20 dollars staked, 20 dollars gone, and an ROI of exactly negative 100 percent, which is the rare number that requires no rounding and no explanation. You cannot get worse than losing everything you put up.

The picks were Florida International minus 10, which finished Middle Tennessee 26, Florida International 23, and Sam Houston plus 3, which finished New Mexico State 30, Sam Houston 24. The model gave those 56 and 57 percent and found edges of 2.1 and 2.6 points. Both lines moved before kickoff, and both moved away from the model, which is zero percent agreement from a market that apparently reads this column.

Season to date sits at 120-143-6 across 269 plays, 2,690 staked, down 241.27, an ROI of negative 9.0 percent against a model expectation of 60 percent. There is one week graded in hindsight that came back 40-25-1 for a 110.47 profit, and picking winners after the scores exist is a hobby, not a result. Five weeks were graded for real. Those are the ones on the receipt.
